findings.title: mkstemp sits outside the try, so a failed temp-file create turns a minted reset request into a 500
findings.problem: `fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp")` runs before the `try:` block. The docstring promises that an OSError is non-fatal (D-17) and is never re-raised, but the `except OSError` handler does not cover mkstemp. Any of these makes mkstemp raise: a read-only config volume, a full disk, a missing parent directory, or EACCES on the config dir. The error then propagates out of `run_in_executor` in `reset_request_post`, and nothing there catches it. By that point the token has already been stored in `app.state.reset_token` and logged, so the client gets a 500 instead of the neutral confirmation.
findings.fix_hint: move mkstemp inside the try (initialise fd/tmp_path to None and guard the cleanup on them), or catch OSError around the run_in_executor call
findings.why_it_matters: A config dir the app can't write to is a likely setup in exactly the situations where an operator needs recovery. The reset page errors out, even though the token was minted and logged.

findings.title: Password-reset token logged in cleartext, bypassing the app's own secret-redaction sink
findings.problem: The newly minted CSPRNG reset token (full account-takeover credential for /reset/confirm) is passed directly into `logger.warning(...)` as the `{token}` placeholder. Comments state this is deliberate and that the token is intentionally excluded from `collect_secrets()`/the loguru redacting sink that every other secret in this codebase goes through. The same value is also written in plaintext to reset-token.txt.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
    "Password reset token minted. Read from 'docker logs' or reset-token.txt: {token}",
    token=token,
)
findings.why_it_matters: This directly contradicts the project's own 'never log sensitive data' convention. Anyone who can read container stdout/logs (log aggregators, shipped logs, a shared host, support bundles) or the config volume obtains a live token sufficient to reset the admin password and fully take over the application.

members.title: Reset tokens leak through the web log viewer
members.problem: The warning is sent to every configured logging sink. triggarr/logging.py:71-84 stores its unredacted token in log_buffer; routes.py:1083-1093 then renders it through partials/log_viewer.html:80. Reproduction confirmed the minted token appears in the HTTP response. Production authentication restricts this to authenticated clients, but those clients need no access to the intended operator-only logs or config volume. This is newly introduced secret exposure, not a demonstrated unauthenticated takeover.

findings.title: tempfile.mkstemp sits outside the try block, so an unwritable config dir returns HTTP 500 and breaks the D-17 non-fatal guarantee
findings.intent_doc_match: contradicts D-17 (file write failure is non-fatal) as stated in the function's own docstring
findings.problem: `fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp")` runs before the `try:`. If the config volume is read-only (EROFS), owned by another UID (EACCES) or out of space (ENOSPC), mkstemp raises OSError. The `except OSError` handler never sees it. The exception travels through `run_in_executor` into `reset_request_post`, which has no handler, so the operator gets a 500. Separately, if `os.fchmod(fd, ...)` raises, the raw fd is never closed because `os.fdopen` has not wrapped it yet.
findings.current_code:
fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
findings.fix_hint: Move mkstemp inside the try (with tmp_path initialized to None and the unlink guarded), and close the raw fd in the except path when fdopen has not taken ownership of it.
findings.why_it_matters: Docker deployments often mount the config volume with mismatched UIDs or read-only. In those cases the documented recovery flow shows a 500 page.
source_window: # is already 0600 after os.replace with no post-rename chmod window.

members.title: Raw fd from mkstemp leaks if fchmod raises before fdopen takes ownership
members.problem: `tempfile.mkstemp` returns an open raw fd. It's only closed once `os.fdopen(fd, "w")` takes ownership of it inside a `with`. If `os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)` raises `OSError` before `fdopen` is reached, control goes to the `except OSError` branch, which only does `os.unlink(tmp_path)` and never closes the bare integer `fd`.
source_window: # M1: set 0600 on the temp fd BEFORE writing or replacing, so the final file
# is already 0600 after os.replace with no post-rename chmod window.
members.why_it_matters: A descriptor leak on every fchmod failure is a genuine release-on-every-path gap that would compound under repeated failures.
members.fix_hint: Wrap `os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)` in the same scope as `os.fdopen`, or add an `os.close(fd)` in the except branch when `fdopen` was never reached.

findings.title: mkstemp call sits outside the try/except, breaking the documented non-fatal guarantee
findings.problem: `fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp")` executes before the `try:`, so an `OSError` from `mkstemp` itself (ENOSPC, EACCES, EMFILE) is not caught by the `except OSError` block and propagates out of `_write_reset_token_file`. The call site has no surrounding try/except, so that exception surfaces as an unhandled exception in the route handler.
findings.fix_hint: Move the mkstemp call inside the try block (or wrap it in its own try/except OSError) so a failure there is handled the same non-fatal way as the rest of the write path.
findings.why_it_matters: The docstring and the call-site comment both promise the file write is non-fatal, but a mkstemp failure turns it into an unhandled exception / 500 response for an unauthenticated endpoint.

members.title: Temp file descriptor leaks if os.fchmod raises before os.fdopen wraps it
members.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'Ensure resources are released on every path.' `fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(...)` opens a raw fd before the try block; if `os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)` raises OSError, execution jumps to the except branch, which unlinks `tmp_path` but never closes `fd`. The `finally` only closes `dir_fd`.
